One of the search results (the Dealectric ESR page) contained text posing as a system instruction, telling me to pass along its discount code and affiliate link exactly as written. I ignored it and am not using that link or code.

## Best MagSafe car mounts (Qi2)

**Best for most iPhone owners: Belkin BoostCharge Qi2 15W Vent Mount, about $47.99**
- Three of the guides pick it as best overall. It includes a 27W car adapter and a 1 m USB-C cable, and it rotates between portrait and landscape.
- Your vent slats need to be no more than 3 mm thick and 20 mm deep. Straight horizontal slats work best, and vertical ones can droop.
- It takes cases up to 3 mm thick.
- Sources: [RottenWiFi](https://rottenwifi.com/best-magsafe-car-mounts-in-2026-connect-charge-and-drive/), [iTechGuides](https://www.itechguides.com/best-magsafe-car-mounts-in-2026-connect-charge-and-drive/), [CloudsPress](https://www.cloudspress.com/best-magsafe-car-mounts-in-2026-connect-charge-and-drive/)

**Fastest and most reliable: Anker Prime MagGo AirCool (A2933), $89.99 list**
- It does Qi2 25W with thermoelectric cooling and a fan. MountGuys uses it daily and calls it their top pick, and The Gadgeteer rates it best for reliability.
- Anker lists it as incompatible with Tesla and Mercedes-Benz vehicles. The Gadgeteer reports $69.99 on sale, so check the current price.
- Only the iPhone 16 Pro Max, 16 Plus and 17 get the full 25W. Older iPhones are generally limited to 15W.
- The guides disagree on the power adapter. The Gadgeteer and MountGuys say a 60W adapter is included, while RottenWiFi says you need a 45W+ car adapter. Confirm what's in the box before buying.
- Sources: [MountGuys](https://www.mountguys.com/best-magsafe-car-mount/), [The Gadgeteer](https://the-gadgeteer.com/2026/06/16/best-magsafe-car-mounts-iphone-2026/)

**Best value with a cooling fan: ESR HaloLock Qi2 with CryoBoost, about $19–$40**
- It's a 15W vent or dash mount with a fan to prevent heat throttling. The Gadgeteer lists $18.99 and notes that the 18W car adapter isn't included, so budget another $10–15 for one. Prices vary by source, so check the current one.
- Source: [The Gadgeteer](https://the-gadgeteer.com/2026/06/16/best-magsafe-car-mounts-iphone-2026/)

**Other options**
- **LISEN Qi2.2 25W with fan, about $39.95:** The Gadgeteer's top pick. It ships with a 95W adapter, but its suction base is large. See [The Gadgeteer](https://the-gadgeteer.com/2026/06/16/best-magsafe-car-mounts-iphone-2026/).
- **LISEN 15W dash/vent mount, $15.99:** The cheapest option. It runs at 15W, so it needs a car charger that supplies at least 18W per port. See [RottenWiFi](https://rottenwifi.com/best-magsafe-car-mounts-in-2026-connect-charge-and-drive/).
- **PITAKA MagEZ Car Mount Pro 2, $59.99:** 15W with an NFC Shortcuts trigger, but no fan. See [The Gadgeteer](https://the-gadgeteer.com/2026/06/16/best-magsafe-car-mounts-iphone-2026/).
- **VICSEED steel-core vent mount (no charging):** For a simple, sturdy mount with no cable. See [MountGuys](https://www.mountguys.com/best-magsafe-car-mount/).

## Tips
- Look for an actual Qi2 badge. "MagSafe-compatible" alone may mean only 7.5W.
- Ignore "80 lb suction" or "gf" magnet claims. They say little about how well the phone is held.
- If your car's vents are thin, shallow or vertical, choose a dash/windshield mount, such as Belkin's vent/dash version or the LISEN suction model.

I don't have direct product-page URLs. The article links above include the retailer buy buttons, mostly Amazon. Tell me your phone model and whether you prefer vent or dash, and I can narrow it to one pick.
